findings.reason: a worker dispatched on this section is fenced out of the file it must edit, and without the shared-checkout path carried across the re-exec the follower serves the materialised commit forever, so the section as written does not deliver its own title.
findings.text: §41's last deliverable bullet ("The code stamp a follower compares reads HEAD's commit rather than the working tree's files") is satisfiable only by changing the stamp's own definition, which lives in `reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:28` (`follower_code_stamp`, resolving the package from `Path(__file__)`) delegating to `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:400` (`code_stamp`); both are outside §41's declared write paths (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, `reckon/checkout_*` only — and §40's write paths did include `obligation_snapshot.py` for its own constants). Worse, the mechanism as written is self-defeating: once the follower re-execs onto the tree materialised for the current commit, `follower_code_stamp()` hashes that frozen copy (`Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`), which never changes when a later merge lands on the shared checkout, so the reloader would see no stamp move and never reload again; and no bullet says how the shared checkout's path survives the re-exec so the stamp can keep reading HEAD.

findings.reason: a case that cannot fail (a working-tree-reading stamp passes it) leaves the stamp change unverified.
findings.text: §41's done-when moves HEAD and leaves a modified tracked file, then asserts only that poll reloads and that the import root holds the second commit's tree; both hold whether the stamp reads HEAD's commit or the working tree's content, because moving HEAD changes both, so the deliverable's bullet that the stamp reads the committed head rather than the working tree's files has no measure and its negative control exercises only the dirty-tree branch.
